content: Synaptotagmin-like protein 1 (SYTL1) is a protein in humans encoded by the SYTL1 gene. Model organisms have been utilized to investigate the function of SYTL1. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Sytl1tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was developed as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program is a high-throughput mutagenesis initiative designed to create and distribute animal models of human diseases to researchers. Both male and female mice from this knockout line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening to assess the effects of the gene deletion. A total of 24 tests were conducted on homozygous mutant mice, and six significant abnormalities were identified. In female mice, abnormalities included impaired locomotor coordination, caudal vertebral transformation, reduced circulating amylase levels, and increased mean platelet volume. Both male and female mice exhibited decreased levels of IgG2b and abnormal parameters in peripheral blood lymphocytes. Additionally, SYTL1 has been demonstrated to interact with the protein RAB27A.
